data.case_title: Suspected scam: fake energy cost refund demanding an upfront fee
data.explanation: This letter claims you are owed a €612 refund for past energy bills, but asks you to first pay a €49.90 "processing fee" to a Cyprus bank account. This is a classic advance-fee scam pattern: unexpected windfall, upfront fee required, foreign account, tight deadline and a threat that the claim "expires forever" if you miss it. A legitimate refund from your actual energy supplier would never require you to pay a fee first. Do not transfer any money and do not reply with personal or bank details. If in doubt, contact your real energy provider directly using contact details from your own contract, or report this letter to the police/consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale).

data.summary: A sender calling itself "Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie" (based in Nicosia, Cyprus) claims that a €612 energy cost refund for 2023–2025 has been approved, but demands a €49.90 "processing fee" paid to a Cypriot account by 27 November 2026 before any refund would be paid out. This pattern (unexpected refund, upfront fee to a foreign account, hard deadline, claim of permanent forfeiture) is a strong indicator of an advance-fee scam.
warnings: This has strong hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: an unsolicited large refund conditioned on first paying a smaller upfront fee.
The payment account is a Cyprus IBAN, unusual for a claimed German energy cost refund and a common red flag for fraud.
The sender's address and contact details (Nicosia, Cyprus; generic .example email) do not match any known legitimate German energy authority or utility.
The letter uses high-pressure language ('verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig') to rush payment before the recipient can verify the claim.
Do not share bank details or make any payment based on this letter; verify independently with your actual energy supplier or local consumer protection office.
